$comment: version 1. FIELD-additive superset of vicario review-findings: extra optional fields are ignored by vicario's validator. The dimension enum is the canonical 9-value SHARED contract (vicario's six + lens's test/risk/comment); vicario adopts the same enum so all dimensions validate both ways — no mapping layer. Until the vicario repo widens its enum to match (tracked), only the 6 shared dimensions round-trip to an un-updated vicario; coordinate enum changes across both repos.
title: lens review-findings

oneOf.$comment: SUCCESS channel — the ordinary return, and the only channel a 1.4.3-shaped call can ever receive. Its required[] is 1.4.3's, unchanged, and the top-level properties below are its field set: declaring the failure channel as a branch rather than as another property is what keeps that field set from growing. `error` is excluded here so the two channels stay mutually exclusive instead of both matching a half-and-half object. The allOf clauses below carry CROSS-FIELD constraints; none adds a property, so the derived seven-field count is untouched. They are NARROWINGS, not additions: each rejects documents 1.4.3's schema accepted, and lens/CHANGELOG.md's 1.5.0 entry discloses them as such.

allOf.$comment: degraded:true ⇒ degradedReasons[] present and non-empty. Stated in prose as 'present if and only if degraded is true', this half was unenforced: an engine that set the bit and named no cause validated, and a consumer branching on degradedReasons[] to learn WHY silently read a partial run as a clean one. NARROWING: degradedReasons did not exist in 1.4.3, so no 1.4.3-produced degraded return satisfies this clause.

degraded:false ⇒ degradedReasons[] absent or empty — the other half of the same biconditional. Without it a return could name causes while claiming full coverage, which is the same contradiction read from the other side.

emptyScope:true ⇒ findings[] empty. emptyScope is declared 'true ONLY on empty-diff/no-repo' and 'the SOLE discriminator between nothing-to-review and a review that found nothing', yet a document setting the flag beside a populated findings[] validated — so the discriminator a caller is told to key on could contradict the array it is meant to replace. NARROWING: emptyScope existed in 1.1.0, so a prior-run document carrying the flag alongside findings no longer validates.

oneOf.$comment: FAILURE channel — the named-error envelope a pre-flight raise returns. Sealed to the single key `error`, so an envelope can never arrive carrying half a review. A consumer branches on the presence of `error` BEFORE it reads either channel; this is not a review-findings document, and vicario's validator is not expected to accept it.

votes.$comment: the verify tally for this finding; total == n (the caller's verifyVotes) and couldNotRefute + refuted + abstained == total. abstained counts the dead votes — verifier runs that errored mid-way. Optional. The four counts carry minimum:0 and total is bounded to verifyVotes' own 1..5 range: a tally is a count of dispatches, so a negative member and a total outside the panel sizes the engine can be asked for are both unreachable states the schema should not accept. NARROWING: votes has existed unbounded since 1.0.0 — not 1.4.3 — so a prior-run document from any release carrying a negative count or a total outside 1..5 no longer validates. The sum invariant itself stays prose — draft-07 cannot express it.

voteResolution.$comment: this finding's outcome under the named rule huginn-quorum-v1, whose procedure is declared in skills/engine/references/pipeline.md §5 and not restated here. 'dropped' is deliberately absent: a dropped finding never reaches findings[], so no surviving finding can carry it. Optional — a finding may omit it.

voteDegraded.$comment: carried for vicario parity; lens v1 does not set it

degradedReasons.$comment: Optional, engine-owned. degraded:true if and only if this array is non-empty (enforced by the success branch's allOf, not left to prose); the closed 7-code set is declared in skills/engine/references/engine-api.md, not restated here.

items.$comment: `code` is required and the object is sealed, matching how definitions.errorEnvelope is sealed. Untightened, {} and {"detail":"…"} and a typo'd {"cod":"finder-died"} all validated — so the closed enum guarded nothing, and a consumer branching on the code read every degrade as an unrecognized one.

emptyScope.$comment: true only on empty-diff/no-repo; lets a caller distinguish 'nothing to review' from a clean zero-finding review. Field-additive — vicario's validator ignores it (only the dimension enum is co-owned).

severityTrend.$comment: this run's recommendedEscalation vs the prior run's, keyed on the 4-value escalation not the 3-value verdict (per skills/review/references/reconcile.md). Optional — set by reconcile/compute-only, never by the engine; vicario's validator ignores it.

delta.$comment: aggregate iteration delta vs the prior run; read by an orchestrator's convergence decision and surfaced as the human-facing iteration delta. Optional — set by reconcile/compute-only, never by the engine.

adherence.$comment: Optional, field-additive — set by the finders' side outputs or the engine's adherence return; vicario's validator ignores it. Item objects declare their known keys but stay open (no required[], no additionalProperties:false) so single-spec flat items and headless-derived items — which may omit sourceSpec/sourcePlan — remain valid.

errorEnvelope.$comment: the envelope's shape AND its closed code set. skills/engine/references/engine-api.md § Errors stays the single DECLARED home — the raiser, the trigger and the per-code `extra` shape are only there, and the two invariants that bound the channel are only there. The four spellings are MIRRORED here on purpose, exactly as degradedReasons' seven-code enum is: an unmirrored `code: string` accepted E_MADE_UP, so the closed registry guarded nothing a validator could see. The mirror is a second COPY, not a second source of truth, and it is pinned back to the § Errors table by tests/lens/test_schema_types.sh so the two can never drift apart silently. Widening this enum is the same ask-first boundary as widening the table.
